name: Old Dominion Eats: Virginia
subtitle: Ham Biscuits, Oysters & Pollo
description:
Virginia's restaurants, from a country ham biscuit to a dozen on the half shell by the bay.

Old Dominion Eats is a free guide to eating in Virginia: 7 biscuit and country ham kitchens, 10 oyster bars, 7 classic counters and diners, 6 pollo a la brasa and pupusa places, 8 pho, banh mi and Korean barbecue restaurants and 4 wine and hunt country tables we checked by hand, plus 17,486 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 473 towns, from Richmond and Norfolk to Northern Virginia and the Cumberland Gap. No account, no ads.

VIRGINIA GUIDES
• Biscuits & Country Ham: biscuit kitchens and country ham, from Wakefield to Leesburg.
• Oyster Bars: raw bars from the Chesapeake to the Blue Ridge.
• Classic Counters & Diners: lunch counters kept going for generations.
• Pollo a la Brasa & Pupusas: Northern Virginia's charcoal chicken and pupusas.
• Pho, Banh Mi & Korean BBQ: from the Eden Center to Annandale.
• Wine & Hunt Country: tables in wine and hunt country.
• MICHELIN & James Beard and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "ham biscuit", "oysters", "pho falls church".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source or the Virginia Tourism Corporation's own listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists. Virginia posts no letter grades; Fairfax-area places show the Fairfax Health District's latest result in its own words with the date, and every place links the Virginia Department of Health's inspection portal. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Old Dominion Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the Commonwealth of Virginia, the Virginia Department of Health or the Fairfax Health District), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Old Dominion Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Virginia (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: ham biscuits, oyster bars, classic counters, pollo a la brasa and pupusas, pho and Korean barbecue and hunt-country tables, 42 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 17,486 restaurants, cafés and bars in 473 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Biscuits & Country Ham (or Oyster Bars, Classic Counters & Diners, Pollo a la Brasa & Pupusas, Pho, Banh Mi & Korean BBQ, Wine & Hunt Country, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, Fairfax-area places show the Fairfax Health District's latest inspection result with its date, and a link opens the Virginia Department of Health's inspection portal in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("ham biscuit", "oysters", "pho falls church").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Virginia (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Virginia, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Old Dominion Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Old Dominion Eats: Virginia".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Old Dominion Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the Fairfax Health District's food permits and inspections (public records); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/virginia-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Virginia; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection results appear only for the Fairfax Health District, in its own words with the date; the app computes no grades and ranks nothing by inspections. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
